newsitem.title: USA: U.S. abortion pill sponsor loses manufacturer - Post.
newsitem.headline: U.S. abortion pill sponsor loses manufacturer - Post.

text.p: A European company that had agreed to manufacture the French abortion pill RU-486 for sale in the United States is backing out of the project, the Washington Post reported on Wednesday, quoting unnamed sources.
The newspaper said the non-profit Population Council, the U.S. sponsor of the pill, now must try to find a replacement manufacturer.

Sandra Waldman, a spokeswoman for the New York-based council, declined to confirm that the European manufacturer was backing out, but said there was a "dispute...and we're continuing to talk to them, and our commercial partners are very actively looking for other manufacturers."
German chemicals and drugs group Hoechst AG in April said it was transferring all rights for the controversial abortion pill to a former manager and would now cease production of the drug completely.
The pill has been available in Europe for several years and although it was widely acclaimed by women's groups in the United States, it has been rabidly opposed by anti-abortion groups here.

Mifepristone is a synthetic steroid that makes it difficult for a fertilised egg to adhere to the lining of the uterus. When taken with misoprotol, a drug that triggers uterine contractions, the result is an abortion.

Hoechst became linked to the controversial pill when it acquired French drug company Roussel Uclaf years ago. In the United States, Hoechst had transferred the rights for the drug to the Population Council at the request of the U.S. government.

The company that agreed to produce the drug for the council was never named and it was unclear whether the latest development was linked to Hoechst's transfer of the patent rights in April to Edourd Sakiz, a developer of the product.
Sakiz recently retired as supervisory board chairman at Hoechst's French subsidiary Roussel Uclaf.
